label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
**[Your Name]**  
School Bus Driver, Bus 41  
Route 9 – Elementary  
Dayton, Ohio  

**Date:** [Date Submitted]  
**To:** Mrs. Okafor  
**Regarding:** Amara Okafor – Afternoon Run, Tuesday, October 27  
**Response to:** Complaint dated October 29, received from my supervisor on November 3  

Dear Mrs. Okafor,

I am writing to explain what happened on Bus 41 during the afternoon run on Tuesday, October 27, when Amara was returned to Fairmont Elementary instead of being let off at her stop at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street. I understand that this was a frightening afternoon for you. I have grandchildren, and I would be frightened too if I were waiting for one of them and did not know why they had not gotten off the bus. I am sincerely sorry that you went through that.

At the same time, I need to explain clearly why I kept Amara on the bus. I did not see an adult at her stop, and her backpack has a green tag indicating that an adult must be there to meet her. Under the district procedure for kindergarten riders, when no adult is present at the stop, the student stays on the bus and is returned to school, and the school office contacts the parent. My decision was based on that rule and on Amara’s safety. It was not personal, and I was not trying to keep her from you or make your afternoon more difficult.

The scheduled time at Kessler and Brandt was 3:50 p.m. We arrived at approximately 3:52 p.m. I looked for an adult at the stop and did not see anyone at the corner whom I could identify as being there for Amara. We remained there until approximately 3:55 p.m. During that time, I still did not see an adult at the stop.

Your complaint states that you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and that you waved at me. I believe that you were trying to get my attention, but I did not see you. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street, which affected what I could see from the driver’s seat. I am not writing this to argue with you about where you were parked. You may have been waving, and I may still not have been able to see you. Both of those things can be true. What I want on the record is that I did not knowingly ignore you or refuse to respond to you.

At approximately 3:56 p.m., I radioed dispatch and reported the situation. Gloria at dispatch responded and called Fairmont Elementary. I then continued with the route. I still had three more stops and 14 children on the bus. Those children were also my responsibility. I could not park the bus, get off, cross the street, and begin looking around the area or checking parked vehicles while leaving those children unattended. That is not something I will do. I also could not leave Amara at the corner without an adult present. Under the circumstances, keeping her safely on the bus and returning her to the school was the required and appropriate course of action.

I understand that the time between her regular stop and her arrival back at Fairmont must have felt very long to you. I was not delaying out of disregard for you or Amara. I still had to carry out the remaining route safely with the other students on board before returning to the school.

We arrived back at Fairmont Elementary at approximately 4:31 p.m. I did not leave Amara outside or send her in by herself. I walked her into the building personally and left her with Mrs. Petrakis in the office. Amara remained supervised from the time I arrived at her stop until she was with school staff.

Amara was safe and calm during the ride. She was coloring on her folder and even asked whether she could ride more. I told her that we were taking a little extra trip because I wanted to reassure her and keep the situation from becoming scary for her. Her being calm does not mean your concern was unreasonable. You were not on the bus and could not see that she was all right. I mention how she was doing only to give you a complete account and to make clear that she was never left alone or treated unkindly.

Your complaint also states that I drove off laughing. I was not laughing at you, at Amara, or about the situation. As I was pulling out, I was speaking to a fourth-grade student in seat 2 and telling that student to sit back down. Getting students seated and keeping them seated while the bus is moving is part of my job. My attention was on the students and on moving the bus safely. I do not know what the moment looked like from where you were, but there was no laughter directed at you and no intention to dismiss or disrespect you.

I have been a school bus driver for 28 years and have not had a write-up. I am proud of that record, but more importantly, I take seriously the trust that parents place in me every day. Families expect me to bring their children safely to school and back home, and sometimes doing that means following a procedure that is inconvenient or upsetting in the moment. Returning a kindergarten student to school when no adult is visible is one of those situations.

This has happened once before on my route, years ago, with a different family. I followed the same procedure, and that family later thanked me for keeping their child safe. I mention that only to explain that this is a safety practice I have applied consistently. It was not a decision directed at you or Amara.

I respectfully request that the Transportation Department pull and preserve the available bus camera footage for this afternoon run, particularly the period around the Kessler and Brandt stop from approximately 3:50 p.m. to 4:00 p.m., as well as the remainder of the run and our return to Fairmont at 4:31 p.m. I also request that the relevant radio and dispatch timing be reviewed. The camera footage should provide an objective record of the bus at the stop, the amount of time we waited, what was taking place inside the bus, Amara’s condition, and my actions. I understand that a camera may not show everything across the street, but it is important that this complaint be evaluated using all available evidence rather than relying only on two different impressions of the same event. I ask that the footage be retained before it is overwritten in the ordinary course of recordkeeping.

Going forward, I want to prevent this from happening again. When you meet Amara, please wait on the bus side of the street at the stop, where I can see you from the driver’s seat. If you are in your vehicle, please step out before the bus arrives and stand where you are clearly visible. If circumstances make that difficult on a particular day, it may help to contact the school or Transportation office in advance so that arrangements can be communicated to me. For my part, I will continue to look carefully before leaving any kindergarten stop. Being visible outside the vehicle will make it much easier for me to confirm that an adult is there for Amara.

I am sorry for the distress you experienced that afternoon. I am not apologizing for following the kindergarten safety procedure, because I believe leaving Amara without an adult or leaving the other students unattended would have put children at risk. I can stand by the safety decision and still regret that you had a bad and frightening afternoon.

I am glad to continue driving Amara. She was comfortable with me that day, and I want her to continue feeling safe on my bus. I also do not want this complaint to create ongoing tension between us. I see my responsibility as bringing her safely to and from school, and I would like us to resolve this in a way that gives you confidence in what will happen at her stop.

Please place this statement in my file alongside the complaint so that my account, the timeline, and my request for review of the camera footage are part of the record.

Respectfully,

**[Your Name]**  
Driver, Bus 41  
Route 9 – Elementary
